title: Data Center Operations Challenge
summary: Respond to a simulated multi-system incident and produce an evidence-based incident report.
objectives: Apply the operations lifecycle to a synthetic incident involving monitoring, network, cooling, and recent-change clues.
Produce an incident report that documents safe decisions, escalation, verification, and remaining uncertainty.

vocab.def: Compare separate pieces of information to see whether they may be related.
The process of returning a service or system to an expected state.
A later action used to confirm, improve, or prevent recurrence.

sections.heading: The scenario
sections.body: A synthetic operations center receives a network alert, a temperature warning, a service-impact report, and a recent change record. Some clues are relevant and some are noise.

sections.heading: The response
sections.body: Confirm the symptom, inspect the evidence, identify affected systems, prioritize safe actions, escalate where required, verify the simulated recovery, and document what remains uncertain.

sections.heading: The boundary
sections.body: This project assesses classroom reasoning and communication. It does not create a project submission record, lab result, verified competency, credential, or job-readiness fact.

practice.prompt: Use the scenario packet to identify symptoms, evidence, possible causes, safe actions, escalation points, and verification checks.

quiz.question: What is the strongest incident conclusion?
options: A conclusion tied to recorded evidence and a defined verification
The first possible cause that comes to mind
A claim that every alert was causal
A statement that no follow-up is needed
quiz.answer: A conclusion tied to recorded evidence and a defined verification

lab.objective: Complete the simulated multi-system incident response using synthetic data and an incident template.

reflectionPrompt: Which clue was hardest to interpret, and what additional evidence would help?

project.title: Data Center Incident Response Challenge
project.instructions: Use the synthetic incident packet to create a structured incident report. Include the symptom, affected systems, evidence, possible causes, safe action, escalation decision, recovery verification, remaining uncertainty, and follow-up.
submissionOptions: structured incident report from synthetic data
small-group oral handoff with a written summary
project.evidenceBoundary: LESSON COMPLETION ONLY: project submission, review, and competency are separate future domains.

levels: Developing: connects evidence to a decision
Proficient: supports the response with multiple recorded clues
Proficient: distinguishes causal evidence from noise
Developing: chooses a safe response or escalation
Proficient: explains why authorization and impact guide escalation
Proficient: creates a clear handoff with status and uncertainty
Developing: uses a check to verify recovery
Proficient: explains follow-up and remaining uncertainty
